"There are no technicians running these equipments. The court is completely dissatisfied with the report placed on record. The hospitals are facing enormous difficulty in recruiting the necessary doctors and the staff. There is no uniform HR policy of the Delhi Government," the Court said. Justice Prathiba M Singh and Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora The Court went on to observe, “ Judges will come, judges will go, but the hospitals have to function ." The Court was hearing a suo motu case in which it routinely monitors healthcare services in the city's government hospitals. items.title: Hafta 607: Who pays for UPI? Is the UCC even ‘uniform’?
items.summary: This week on Hafta, Abhinandan Sekhri, Manisha Pande and Rinchen Norbu are joined by Anupam Manur, Professor of Economics at the Takshashila Institution, and Mihira Sood, Supreme Court lawyer specialising in women’s rights. The panel opens the discussion by examining the government’s decision to introduce a 0.4% fee on UPI merchant transactions above Rs 2,000, asking what the move means for a payment system that has become central to everyday transactions in India. Anupam Manur acknowledges that UPI generates wider economic benefits, but argues that the current model also creates a problem: who ultimately bears the cost of running the system? He explains that the cost of operating UPI is substantial, while the government subsidises only a portion of it. Manur says, “When UPI came about, India was miles ahead of the world in some sense. It was truly revolutionary.” But he argues that the costs leave new entrants with insufficient incentive, which has affected private-sector innovation. “Private players are just not incentivized to innovate.” The discussion then moves from the economics of UPI to the politics of its messaging. items.title: Karnataka High Court quashes criminal case against Pearson Education's former in-house counsel
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has quashed criminal proceedings against former in-house legal counsel of Pearson Education/ Dorling Kindersley (India) Pvt Ltd, Prashant Kumar Joshi [Prashant Kumar Joshi v State of Karnataka]. By way of an order passed on September 11, Justice HP Sandesh quashed the criminal proceedings against Joshi in a case concerning legal metrology violations by Pearson Education. The Court said that Joshi was not a nominated personnel of the company (under Section 49 of the Legal Metrology Act), responsible for the company's business and conduct. The Court ruled that criminalising the former in-house counsel without the company being a party to the proceedings, would amount to an abuse of process of law. "Nothing is stated in the complaint that this petitioner was in charge of the affairs of the company and he being shown as General Manager (Legal), the question of initiating the criminal prosecution against this petitioner is nothing but an abuse of process, which amounts to miscarriage of justice," the order said. items.title: Karnataka govt bans selfies, reels on college tours, caps trips at 5 days
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Karnataka government has directed government first-grade colleges to prohibit students from taking selfies or shooting reels during educational tours, citing safety concerns, and has capped the duration of excursions, including travel, at five days. The Department of Collegiate Education issued the detailed safety guidelines on September 11 and directed principals to brief students about the restrictions before the start of a tour. Faculty members have also been asked to closely monitor students during excursions. According to the Times of India report , colleges must obtain written approval from the department before organising an educational tour. They must also submit undertakings from students and formal consent from parents along with the tour proposal. Once a tour is approved, its itinerary cannot be changed. Students cannot be taken to locations that are not included in the approved plan. The department has also advised colleges against organising educational tours during the monsoon season.
